newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Mahathir opens SE Asia's tallest tower.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir opens SE Asia's tallest tower.

text.p: Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday opened the Kuala Lumpur Tower, estimated to be the tallest telecommunications tower in Southeast Asia and fourth in the world rankings.
Mahathir said critics who described the 421-metre (1,381- foot) structure as a giant "baby's rattle" were merely envious.
"The fact is we are capable of building this tower and we have the architectural perception that produced a structure more beautiful than the telecommunications towers in developed nations," he said.

The 270 million ringgit ($108 million) structure features a revolving restaurant and an observation platform in the six-storey tower head, as well as telecommunications, television and meterological facilities.
The Kuala Lumpur Tower ranks behind Toronto's CN Tower, Moscow's Ostankino Tower and the Shanghai Tower as the fourth tallest telecommunications tower in the world.
It is one of a series of projects pushed by Mahathir, whose "Vision 2020" is intended as a blueprint for Malaysia becoming a fully-developed country in the next quarter-century.
